Clockwork/coloring correspondence

Colors follow one fixed clock: A = phase 0, B = phase 1/N, C = phase 2/N, and so on. CN = (ABC…) is one forward +1/N-period tick, so a row with Time +k/N has Color CNk. Every action is a forward time skip; none reverses time. Raised numbers in the signature give colour-permutation orders, not time shifts.

Every record now carries the same three-part visual trail: clockwork film, static 2D colouring, then a click-to-load interactive example of a real crystal in the associated polar space group.

31 screwd glide

Diagram symbols

Translation, rotation, screw-axis, mirror, and glide marks on the colouring plates follow crystallographic projection notation.

Notation

The displayed names use Chaim Goodman–Strauss’s coloured-orbifold notation. Across all 68 forward groups it gives 64 cyclic plane-colouring classes. Four types leave the two orientations of the polar fibre unresolved: 4424/◦, 3333/◦, 6326/◦, and 6323/2222. These are four two-to-one fibres, not missing colourings; standard fibrifold notation also identifies each pair under fibre reversal. Four uncovered cases ↗ · hierarchy ↗

17 trivial groupsTime is an independent direct-product factor.

51 nontrivial groupsSome spatial symmetries advance time phase.

Diagram key

Crystallographic generator symbols: visual index

Projected along the clock axis, these are the actual symbols used on the static 2D diagrams. Open arrows mark primitive translations in the picture; the crystallographic filled core shows the 2-, 3-, 4-, or 6-fold spatial order. For a forward skip τ, the screw subscript is m ≡ nτ (mod n) for a positive 1/n-turn and m ≡ −nτ (mod n) for the opposite turn, with 0 ≤ m < n. Mirrored blades record spatial turn sense—not backward time.

Translations in the projection plane

  • Primitive translationOpen arrow; its direction is the named in-plane translation X, Y, or α.

Rotation and screw axes (along the clock axis)

  • 2-fold rotation axisFilled lens; half-turn with no clock-axis rise.
  • 21 screw axisTwo-arm lens; half-turn with a +1/2-period rise.
  • 3-fold rotation axisFilled triangle; one-third turn with no clock-axis rise.
  • 31 screw axisThree-stroke triangle; positive one-third turn with a +1/3-period rise.
  • 32 screw axisOpposite three-stroke triangle; positive one-third turn with a +2/3-period rise.
  • 4-fold rotation axisFilled diamond; quarter-turn with no clock-axis rise.
  • 41 screw axisFour-arm diamond; positive quarter-turn with a +1/4-period rise.
  • 42 screw axisTwo-arm diamond; quarter-turn with a +1/2-period rise.
  • 43 screw axisOpposite four-arm diamond; positive quarter-turn with a +3/4-period rise.
  • 6-fold rotation axisFilled hexagon; one-sixth turn with no clock-axis rise.
  • 61 screw axisSix-arm hexagon; positive one-sixth turn with a +1/6-period rise.
  • 62 screw axisThree-arm hexagon; positive one-sixth turn with a +1/3-period rise.
  • 63 screw axisTwo-arm hexagon; one-sixth turn with a +1/2-period rise.
  • 64 screw axisOpposite three-arm hexagon; positive one-sixth turn with a +2/3-period rise.
  • 65 screw axisOpposite six-arm hexagon; positive one-sixth turn with a +5/6-period rise.

Mirror and glide planes (seen edge-on)

  • Mirror plane (m)Solid line; reflection with no glide component.
  • In-plane axial glideDashed line; reflection plus a half-cell step in the picture.
  • Clock-axis glide (c)Dotted line; reflection plus a half-period step perpendicular to the picture.
  • Diagonal n-glideDash–dot line; half-steps in the picture and along the clock axis.
  • Quarter-diagonal d-glideArrowed dash–dot line; arrows select the sign of the quarter-period component.

The burgundy α, β, γ, … or P, Q, … beside a diagram symbol identifies its Generator row. The Color and Time columns state the same forward clock action directly.

Notation: International Tables for Crystallography projection symbols · UCL P 3 1 c example.
